Subject: Performance validation evidence and proposed test matrix (RFP-5782)

Liam / Anita,

Thanks for sharing the RFP. Attached is an initial performance evidence packet and a proposed test matrix tailored to the workload characteristics you included (short chat-style prompts with occasional long-context policy queries). Key notes up front:

- We provide token-level latency breakdowns, sequence-length conditioned P50/P95/P99, and throughput curves across reserved replica counts.
- The attached redwood-performance-matrix.xlsx maps each RFP requirement to the specific artifact we are providing (raw logs, test scripts, run parameters).
- For reproducibility we included qps-test-scripts.zip (k6 + simple harness) and r12-latency-raw-logs.tar.gz (sanitized traces).

Ask: please confirm the target concurrency envelope you want validated during your acceptance window. We propose a 1-hour sustained run at 400 concurrent chat sessions (mix: 75% short, 25% long prefix), then a 30-minute burst phase at 1200 concurrent sessions to exercise cache/fallback behavior.

Attached: redwood-performance-matrix.xlsx; r12-latency-raw-logs.tar.gz; qps-test-scripts.zip

I will loop Dev in for any low-level questions on how the KV-prefetch and batching were configured for the runs. If the window looks good, we can schedule the live handoff and provide a short runbook for your SI team to replay locally.

Thanks,

--

Kimberly,

Thanks for the packet — appreciate the level of detail. A couple of clarifying items before we lock the acceptance test window:

1) Can you confirm whether the burst at 1200 concurrent sessions was run against a single region endpoint or multi-region fronting? We need to understand cross-region failover behavior.
2) For the raw logs: does the r12 archive include per-request kernel-level timing (NTP-aligned) or are timings relative to the service clock? Our auditors need absolute timestamps.
3) On cache warmup: you mention KV-prefetch. Can you provide the steady-state cache hit rate you observed during the sustained 1-hour run?

Also, our procurement team prefers the acceptance window to be on a Tuesday to coordinate with internal staff. Do you have availability the week of Jan 19?

Best,

Subject: Re: Performance validation evidence and proposed test matrix (RFP-5782)

Hi Liam — quick answers, plus details you can pass to your audit team:

- Burst topology: the 1200-concurrency runs used a single-region configuration (us-west-2) on Dedicated capacity to isolate network variability. We ran a separate multi-region failover smoke test (replicated traffic to eu-west-1) and included the results in the appendix of the spreadsheet (tab: geo-failover).

- Timestamps: r12-latency-raw-logs.tar.gz contains NTP-synced timestamps (ISO-8601) captured at the service ingress point. There is a small delta table in the artifact describing clock sync drift (<3ms observed). Those raw files are sanitized for customer identifiers but preserve absolute time.

- Cache metrics: steady-state prefix/KV cache hit rate during the 1-hour steady run was 87%. During the burst phase hit rate dropped to ~62% before the prefix rehydration stabilized (we include per-minute hit-rate time series).

A couple of other technical clarifications: we used quantized model variants for the high-concurrency runs (int8 profile) and the test matrix notes the model hash and quantization profile used. The qps-test-scripts include the exact seeding to reproduce request mix.

If useful, Benchmark Labs (cc'd) can run an independent replay using the same harness; we are happy to coordinate.

Regards,

Dev Patel
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Liam — to confirm next steps and proposed schedule:

1) Acceptance window: Tue, Jan 20 (US business hours). We will reserve Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and provide a read-only dashboard link for your monitoring team.
2) Artifacts: we will deliver a signed checksum for r12-latency-raw-logs and provide a short verification script (sha256sum) prior to the run.
3) Replay options: Benchmark Labs can run an independent replay the morning of Jan 20; their results will be shared directly with your auditors.
4) Test plan: we will execute the 1-hour steady-state then 30-minute burst as described. If Northbridge wants, we can add a 15-minute graceful-failure scenario with an induced replica drain to demonstrate fallback and model-variant degradation behavior.

Please confirm: (A) Jan 20 works for Northbridge, and (B) whether you want the additional graceful-failure scenario. Once confirmed we'll share the runbook and an access calendar invite.

Attachments: updated redwood-performance-matrix.xlsx (version 2)

Appreciate the collaboration — we want the acceptance test to be deterministic and auditable for your procurement and compliance teams.
